  §2.11.
- **16 September 2026** — **Magic move.** The house name for one highlight that
  slides between rows rather than each row painting its own; adopted as the
  term for the tab pill and the profile switcher's fill too, which were the
  same idea by other names. Also extended to the nav rail in `hover` mode, with
  the active fill left untouched. Four new tests in `e2e/header.spec.ts`, each
  confirmed red: the transition removed, the fill painted in the active colour,
  and the rows' own hover restored. Two more followed once it was in use: the
  rail's 8px inter-row gap went, because the fill was crossing dead space on
  every move and the gaps broke the column into seven plates, and the chevron and ⌘D keycap gained a
  500ms delay so running the pointer down the column stops flashing a hint
  on every row. Then the gap went entirely rather than moving inside the
  rows and came back as the same 8px expressed as padding inside them, and the
  hover text darkening was removed so the fill is the only thing a hover
  changes. Two shapes were tried and reverted on the way: 36px rows, and 4px
  of spacing. The rail ends up looking as it always did, with the hole gone.
  All confirmed red, including that the original `gap-[8px]` fails the
  contiguity half while being pixel-identical. One unrelated fix fell out
  of it, in two parts. `e2e/popup.spec.ts`'s frame recorder counted a fixed 30
  frames from when it was installed, so under five competing workers the move
  could begin after they were spent; it records until the value settles now.
  That was not the whole of it: the real failure was `goto` resolving before
  hydration, so a click reached a trigger with no handler and the popup never
  opened. The block waits for a control to be interactive first. Measured at
  roughly one full-suite run in three before, and twelve of thirteen green
  after. Note for anyone editing those: a synthetic `pointerover` moves the
  rail's highlight but *not* a select's or combobox's, which track the pointer
  internally, so those must be driven by a real hover.
- **16 September 2026** — **The menu highlight moves.** One fill per popup,
  translated between rows instead of painted on each: `useMagicMove` /
  `MagicMove` in `ui/magic-move.tsx`, wired into the dropdown menu, the select
  and the combobox, on the Panel tier. §1.7a carries the four rules and the
  three endpoint-invisible causes; `e2e/popup.spec.ts` counts the frames in
  between, confirmed red on removing the transition and again on swapping the
  callback ref for a plain one.
- **16 September 2026** — **Two table rules, both on the footer.** Its right
  padding is 8px against the left's 36px, because the pager's ghost buttons
  carry their own padding and 36px on top of it pushed the last arrow off the
  card's corner: padding to a control is not padding to a letterform. And the
  go-to-page box is filled `bg-raised`, two steps off the band, where it had
  been transparent until hovered and so read as the counter beside it rather
  than as something you can type into. The fill is a role and not a step
  because the ramp runs opposite ways per theme, which is what §1.1 exists to
  let us say. Both measured in the browser in both themes and confirmed red on
  reverting each independently.
- **16 September 2026** — **The pager's box came down to one shade.** Two was
  too strong on the footer. `--sidebar-field` is a new token rather than a
  reused role, because "one step off `--sidebar`" is not a value any existing
  role holds in both themes: `--muted` is one step in light and three in dark.
  gray-100 in light, gray-900 in dark, stepping up rather than down because
  gray-950 is the ramp's floor. The browser check gained an upper bound with
  it, since the rule it now guards is a value that was already once too dark.
- **16 September 2026** — **Sorting became opt-in, and the clause library lost
  it.** The clause library showed sort arrows on hover with no eye anywhere on
  the page to hide them, and so did the employees list: `RecordTable` sorted by
  default while `SortToggle` lives in a `FilterBar` neither of them has. A
  control and the thing that governs it are one unit, so the half `RecordTable`
  can carry is now the half that waits to be asked for. Documents and clients
  are unaffected, since passing an order implies the opt-in and both already
  render the eye. Enforced per feature folder, and the first version of that
  rule was **wrong in a way worth recording**: it let a table fall back to its
  parent folder's toggle, so removing the clients eye left it green. Folder-only
  now, and confirmed red on both real tables.
- **17 September 2026.** **A body row grows with its text, and drags by a
  grip.** The clause body editor's rows were `rows={2}` plus `resize-y`: a
  two-line floor on every row whatever it held, and a drag corner in each
  corner. Both are answers to a question `field-sizing-content` had already
  answered on the primitive, so the fix was deleting two overrides rather than
  adding anything. Rows start at the 36px rung and grow (§2.2), and the rule is
  now enforced, with the nine files that already broke it grandfathered rather
  than swept: that judgement wants making per form, with the form on screen.

  **The rule's first version was wrong in a way worth recording.**
  `<Textarea[^>]*rows=` cannot cross a `>`, so it stopped at the first arrow
  function in the props and read as passing on the very file it was written
  for, catching only the tags whose attributes came in a lucky order. It is
  matched per tag then per attribute now. A rule confirmed red against *some*
  violation is not confirmed: it has to be the one in front of you.

  Same pass: the two move chevrons became one `GripVertical` that drags with a
  pointer **and** moves on the arrow keys, because a handle alone is unreachable
  by keyboard and this is the form for editing the words of an agreement. The
  drawer's title became the clause's heading (the number says nothing about
  which clause is open and now sits in the pager), the standing line under it
  went, and a **clause pager** took the centre of the control row: previous,
  the number, next, walking by position rather than by number because a number
  is never reissued and arithmetic would page into a gap. Paging flushes the
  autosave first, like archive and delete do.

  **A panel's state belongs to the panel, not to what is inside it.** The pager
  shipped with a bug that is worth keeping written down: `expanded` sat in the
  drawer, and the drawer is keyed by clause number so that a new clause arrives
  with its own draft and its own parsed body. Paging therefore remounted it, and
  expanding then paging dropped the reader out of the full panel and back into a
  side drawer, mid-read. The key is correct and stays; the state moved up to the
  list, which owns which clause is open and now also owns how the panel is
  shown. The general form: **a remount key is a statement about identity, so any
  state that should outlive a change of identity has to live above it.** Cleared
  on close, or state lifted up outlives the thing it described.

  Then the title took `text-base` and the header lost its rule. "About 4px
  bigger" is 18px by arithmetic and there is no 18px: §1.4 is four sizes and
  says a fifth is a mistake rather than a nuance, so it lands on 16, the
  card/section heading rung, which is what a panel title is. **A size request
  resolves to the nearest rung, not to the number**; where the gap is too wide
  for that to satisfy the request, the scale is what wants revisiting, in its
  own change.
- **17 September 2026.** **A drawer can float, and the clause drawer does**
  (§2.11). `SheetContent` gained `float`: inset from all four of the card's
  edges, `rounded-sm`, ringed, and centred at `lg` rather than merely wider.
  Flush stays the default, because a feed dropping from the edge belongs
  against it.

  **The scrim and the float are one decision, not two.** The clause drawer's
  backdrop went 80% to 25% to transparent to a weight that follows the panel's
  size, all in one day, each step for the same reason: a clause is read against
  its neighbours, which cite it by number. What the passes kept discovering is
  that an undimmed page leaves a flush panel with no edge at all, worst in dark
  mode where the sheet's surface and the inset behind it are close in lightness
  and the shadow does not read. Floating answers that, so the panel carries its
  own boundary; fully transparent then proved a step too far, because a panel
  over an entirely untouched page reads as being *in* it. It settled at 10% as
  a drawer and 40% expanded (§2.11). **The backdrop element is never deleted**,
  whatever its weight: it catches the outside click and keeps the page inert.

  Confirmed red with `float` removed: the panel measured flush on three edges
  and 128px off centre when expanded. Also this pass: the control row lost its
  bottom border, expand took Lucide's `Maximize`, and each control's tooltip
  became one word while its `aria-label` kept its object, the two being read in
  different contexts (§1.5). **`ConfirmActionButton` gained `tooltip`** for the
  one control in that row that had none, which was also the only irreversible
  one.
- **17 September 2026** — **A sheet takes one of three sizes.** There were three
  drawers and three unrelated answers to how wide a drawer is: the notifications
  feed took the base `sm:max-w-sm`, the clause drawer overrode it to
  `sm:max-w-xl`, the mobile nav set a CSS variable. `size` is 30/60/90% of the
  inset card, percentages rather than maxima because a contained sheet resolves
  against a card whose width moves with the sidebar. A hand-typed width now
  fails the build. **The floors were the part that had to be measured**: `md`
  was set to `min-w-2xl` from the size's name, and since the card is 1028px at a
  1280 viewport, that 672px floor sat above 60% and silently governed the whole
  laptop range. Each floor is now under what its share yields on the narrowest
  real screen, except `sm`, which deliberately holds 384px so the feed never
  gets narrower than the fixed width it replaced.
- **17 September 2026** — **`devIndicators: false`.** Next's dev-tools portal
  pins itself to the viewport corner the header's last control sits in: at
  1280px the notifications bell is at x=1240 and `elementFromPoint` on its
  centre answered `NEXTJS-PORTAL`, so three sheet specs timed out on a button
  they could see, that was enabled and stable, and that nothing would let them
  click. Dev-only, so nothing a user meets changes; in the config rather than
  worked around in Playwright, because the collision is with the page.
- **17 September 2026** — **`components/flow/` extracted from onboarding**, with
  no behaviour change: the three-band layout, the step row, the submit portal,
  the finish moment and the four form helpers. Onboarding was the only wizard in
  the app, so all of it lived inside `ClientOnboarding`; the contract builder
  needed the same frame, and copying it would have been two sets of answers
  about locking, announcing and where the button sits. 555 lines left that file
  against 93 added, and **its twelve test files were not touched**, which is what
  proves the move: 135 assertions passing against code they never mention. The
  shell gained two props onboarding does not use, `fill` and `rightAction`, for
  a phase that is its own layout. Enforced: `aria-current="step"` outside
  `components/flow/` fails the build, seen red while `StepNav` was still in the
  onboarding file.
- **17 September 2026** — **The contract is built in five phases, not a rail.**
  `ContractEditor` (686 lines, three stages in local state) became
  `contract/flow/` on `FlowShell`: client, services, scope, terms, preview, with
  the phase in the URL. The old file argued against that ("a remount would throw
  it away"), which held for a component whose stages shared one unsaved
  `useState` and does not here: autosave writes on every change and
  `router.replace` does not remount. Services now seed from the client record
  (`PRINCIPLES.md` rule 3, the invoice's precedent at `CONTEXT.md` §5i), and
  telling the record about a service added on a contract is a separate explicit
  act that never removes.
- **17 September 2026** — **A door guard became a ledger, and it needed two
  signals.** `ServiceDialog` refused to commit a Part until every blank was
  filled, which made "complete or not at all" true by construction; seeded Parts
  never pass through that button, so the guarantee moved to phase 3 and the form
  (now a 60% sheet beside the list it came from) saves what is in front of it.
  The count is derived from `contractScopes`, the enumeration finalize reads, so
  the ledger can never disagree with the guard. **Measured while building it: 21
  of the 22 seeded Services have no blank outside their fee**, so a derived count
  alone would have waved almost every service straight through — which is why a
  Part is also confirmed by hand, the one piece of stored state here, gating the
  phase and never finalize.
- **17 September 2026** — **The standing terms lost their dividers.** Thirteen
  figures sat in seven sections, two of which spent a heading, a separator and a
  whole row on one input. One grid per group instead: 28 figures land in 9 rows
  on a two-Schedule contract. The clause headings were checked before they went
  rather than assumed redundant — all thirteen `blankMeta` titles already name
  their own clause and none collide.
- **17 September 2026** — **The pager's pages became a tab group.** A trough
  with the current page raised on it, replacing a "Page 3 / 9" readout between
  two arrows where every page but the two either side of you took a click each.
  Up to six pages every page is a button and there are no arrows and no box;
  past six it is three runs (first, a sliding window of four, last) gapped 8px,
  with runs merged where they touch so no number is ever drawn twice and no gap
  ever falls between neighbours. The arrow still means "next page" and the
  window turns in batches behind it. The arithmetic is `ui/pageGroups.ts`, pure
  and separately tested, because every hard case here is a number rather than a
  box. **Two things fell out of it:** the trough had to be `bg-sidebar-field`
  rather than the tab list's `bg-muted`, since `--raised` and `--muted` are the
  same ramp step in dark and the active page was invisible but for its border
  (caught in a browser, now measured in both themes); and `onPrev`/`onNext` are
  gone, because the box already went through `onGoToPage` and every caller
  pointed all three at one function, so the "the preview scrolls where a table
  swaps" distinction they existed for was never real.
- **17 September 2026** — **The component library, at `/client/library`.** The
  place a component is decided: a rail of components, and one component's
  variants live and drivable beside it. It imports the real primitive, so there
  is no second step where a change ships and no second copy to disagree with the
  app. Pagination is its first and only entry, with the four shapes it takes at
  the lengths that produce them. It supersedes `/admin/kit`, a flat scroll of
  static examples with no way to drive any of them, which stays until its six
  sections are re-homed one at a time. **Three things the page itself taught,
  all in the browser:** the trailing merge was invisible until a specimen opened
  on the last page, since every long list shows the leading one on open; an
  empty stage reads as a broken render unless it says it is empty on purpose;
  and a specimen must be drawn on the band the component ships onto, which is a
  mistake only dark mode can show, because `--card` and `--sidebar` are
  indistinguishable in light. **The e2e spec was vacuous when written** and is
  recorded as such in its own header: it compared each element's own
  `background-color`, the pager's `<nav>` has none, so transparent matched
  transparent and it passed against a specimen moved to the wrong surface
  entirely.
- **17 September 2026** — **The pager became one control rather than five.**
  Both arrows, both anchors and the window now sit in a single container, and
  nothing inside it carries a stroke: it was three troughs with the arrows loose
  outside them, five separate objects saying one thing. The active page moved to
  `--card` (gray-50 in light, as specified) with its border kept, an inactive
  one is bare until hovered, and the pill is rounded tighter than the box so the
  nesting reads. **One thing fell out of it and needed its own fix:** the 8px
  gap between runs stopped meaning anything. It worked while each run had a
  trough, because the space between two backgrounds is a boundary; with one
  container the background groups everything together and the gap became
  indistinguishable from loose tracking, so `‹ 1 9 10 11 12 23 ›` read as one
  continuous list. That is §2.10's own lie, arrived at from the opposite
  direction. A hairline now stands in each gap, never after the last run, and
  none is drawn where two runs are merged. Caught in a browser; the Jest tests
  were all green.
- **17 September 2026** — **The go-to box joined the container, and the dark
  pill got its fill back.** Three corrections to the pass above, each from
  looking at the thing rather than at the numbers. The box was left outside on
  the reasoning that a field you type into is a different kind of thing from a
  page you can be on: true of the control, false of the layout, since it moves
  with the pager and floating beside it read as a second widget that happened to
  be adjacent. It is `--hover`, a step *down* from the container while every
  other filled thing steps up, which is the difference between a well and a
  pill. The active page was `--card` in both themes, and `--card` is the
  container's own value in dark, so its fill separated by **0.000** and the
  border alone was drawing it; `dark:bg-raised` restores +0.91 while light keeps
  gray-50 as specified. And the run separator moved off `--border` (white at
  10% in dark, fainter than the frame around it) onto the text ramp at 40%,
  then came *down* from 18px to 12px: weight and height are separate knobs and
  only weight should have been doing the work, since a full-height rule read as
  a structural divider cutting the control into sections.
- **17 September 2026** — **The pager's active page got its own token, and dark
  went two steps up.** `--page-active` (gray-50 / gray-700) replaces the
  `bg-card` plus `dark:bg-raised` pair that was describing one surface with two
  names. Dark is gray-700 rather than the symmetrical gray-800, on request:
  3.04 against the container where gray-800 gave 0.91, and 0.000 before that
  when both were `--card`. The note in `globals.css` refusing gray-700 for
  `--hover` was checked rather than assumed to apply: it is about
  `--muted-foreground` at 3.94:1 on a hovered card, and this pill prints
  `--foreground` at 9.71:1. Added to `contrast.test.ts` and seen red against a
  value pushed up the ramp until the text stopped clearing AA.
- **17 September 2026** — **The ⌘D palette's cards share one moving fill**, the
  magic move's third caller and the first that is a grid. Two rules came out of
  the shape rather than out of the colour. **One fill serves the pointer and
  the keyboard cursor**, the opposite of the nav rail, because a rail's active
  fill says which page you are on while a palette's selection is only a cursor:
  hovering a card selects it, and Enter opens whatever the fill sits on.
  **And the focus ring had to be taken off `focus-visible:`.** Selecting a card
  focuses it, which is what makes Enter work, but a programmatic `.focus()`
  inherits the modality the dialog was entered with, so Chromium painted the
  keyboard ring for a mouse move: measured in both themes, with the ring
  chasing the pointer across the grid. The card records what moved the
  selection and the ring follows that instead. Two e2e tests in
  `e2e/popup.spec.ts`, both confirmed red, and the second catches something no
  existing caller could: pinning `left` to 0 in the hook leaves all four popup
  tests green and fails only the palette's landing test, because every other
  caller is a list of full-width rows where the horizontal axis never moves.
  Then the grid's own scrolling had to be fixed to match: five cards do not
  fit, so hovering the clipped bottom row lifted it into view with a hard snap
  under a fill that was gliding. `scroll-behavior: smooth` does not fix that,
  which was measured rather than assumed, because a focus scroll ignores the
  property; `focus({ preventScroll: true })` plus `scrollIntoView` does. Two
  more tests, both seen red. The second exists because the blanket
  reduced-motion rule in `globals.css` cannot reach a behavior passed as an
  argument, so this scroll kept animating for somebody who asked it not to
  while every CSS transition in the app correctly stopped. One test was wrong
  before the code was: `hover()` scrolls its own target into view, so it was
  measuring Playwright rather than the palette, and failed against a fix that
  worked.
- **17 September 2026** — **A 36px rung, and the clause drawer resized around
  it.** The drawer's Heading and Description were the compact 32px under a
  full-width body editor and the three add-a-paragraph buttons were `form`
  (38px), which is the size for a button sitting *inline with* an Input: these
  sit in a row of their own with no field beside them, so it only made them the
  largest thing on the panel. Fields to 36, buttons to 28 (`default`, the dense
  height this tool is built at). The conflict was named before it was built,
  because §2.2 fixed the ladder at two values on purpose, and the answer chosen
  was a real rung rather than a one-off class. So `md` exists on all five
  typed-into primitives, not on the `Input` that needed it: a height declared by
  one control is how a field row comes out two heights the day a select joins
  the form. `control-size.test.tsx` holds the five together and was confirmed
  red with one of them missing the rung; the drawer's own measurements are in
  `e2e/clause-library.spec.ts`, since jsdom resolves no stylesheet and any size
  would pass there. The citations and those three buttons then joined one band,
  "Refers to" at the left and the buttons at the right end, which also recovered
  a row of the drawer's height. Two things it is worth knowing the shape of:
  the buttons became their own export rather than moving into `ClauseLibrary`,
  so the `add` logic stays where the parts are and only the layout moved, and
  they are deliberately **not** nested inside `ClauseCitations`, which renders
  `null` for a clause that cites nothing and would have taken them with it. The
  row uses `mr-auto` on an always-rendered left slot rather than
  `justify-between`, because `justify-between` with one child pushes that child
  left: on the clauses that cite nothing the buttons landed at x=806 against a
  right edge of 1262, caught by the test written for exactly that case.
- **17 September 2026** — **The clause drawer lost its Save button and gained a
  control row.** Five controls above the title, ordered by what each acts on:
  leaving (back), then the panel (expand), then, pushed right, the clause in
  rising order of consequence (download, archive, delete). Four things about it
  are decisions rather than defaults. **Autosave is debounced at 800ms, and the
  debounce is the safety mechanism rather than a tweak**: this file said
  "saved explicitly, not autosaved" on the argument that a clause is the source
  text for every contract drafted afterwards, and waiting for the typing to stop
  is what answers that argument rather than discarding it. The conflict was
  raised before it was built. **Delete keeps its confirmation**, and needs it
  more than before: an icon in a row is easier to hit by accident than the
  labelled button it replaced. **Expand is one toggle, not two buttons**, taking
  the sheet's existing `lg` (90% of the inset), so there is never an inert
  control and no second component to keep in step. **The sheet's own close X is
  off**, because the back arrow does that job. That last one was a real bug
  caught by eye in a screenshot: left on, the X sat *over* the delete icon, two
  controls in one corner and one of them irreversible. Pinned by hit-testing the
  delete button rather than by counting buttons, which would pass with the two
  stacked, and confirmed red against the overlap. The Markdown download is
  `domain/contract/clauseMarkdown.ts`, pure and tested there, with three lines
  of Blob plumbing in the drawer.


---

# Part 2: docs/service-catalogue.md

> The spec the 16 services and 293 items are generated from.

# Service catalogue: the complete structure

> **This document is the spec, and the seed is written from it.** Nothing in the
> service system is built until this file is right: the previous attempt guessed
> the structure and produced a catalogue that reached no document.
>
> Companion files: `contract-system.md` holds the four Schedules and the 22 legal
> Parts; `contract-content.md` holds their text. This file holds **what is sold**.
>
> Every rate and unit below is **transcribed from the five rate-card PDFs** via
> `scripts/rate-card-menu.json`, which holds all 278 lines. Nothing is invented.
> Decisions are marked **[DECISION]**; unresolved questions **[OPEN]**. Ten
> questions were put to the founder and nine closed on 19 September 2026; §8
> records each answer and what is still open.

Status: **proposed, 19 September 2026.** Not yet built. §8 lists the one
remaining open question, which does not block the build.

---

## 1. Why this exists

### The diagnosis

One concept is modelled as three half-overlapping ones.

1. **The 22 services** (`src/lib/domain/contract/seed/services.ts`) were
   transcribed from `contract-content.md`. They are **contract Parts by origin**:
   legal scope units with `[blanks]`, limits, completion criteria and exclusion
   ids. They were never a sales catalogue.
2. **`included[]`** is contract prose parsed for `[blanks]` against an exact key
   set in `blankMeta.ts`. A form may not write to it: shifting an ordinal moves a
   client's stored figure onto a different sentence.
3. **`menu[]`** (18 September 2026, commit `7f4eb9a`) holds 278 priced rate-card
   lines and **is read by nothing outside the services admin screen**: no reader
   exists under `src/components/docs/`, `src/components/contract/` or
   `src/lib/domain/contract/`. `MenuLine.id`'s never-reissue rule exists to
   protect `ClientEngagedService.menuIds`, **a field that was never added**.

The rate cards were poured into a structure that could not carry them, and the
data proves it: `rate-card-menu.json` files **88 of its 278 lines under service
`06`** while services `02` and `05` get none, and **18 of its 46 groups span more
than one service** (`Foundation system` → 01 and 06; `Retainership` → 18, 19, 20).
The `_review` block at the top of that file is the previous session listing seven
filing problems it could not resolve. The filing is not wrong; the shape is.

### Already written down

`ROADMAP.md` §10, reported 3 September 2026 while onboarding a real client, names
the same sub-items ("analytics, CRO, a CMS, interactivity... cookie consent,
3D/WebGL, booking systems, payment gateway integration") and instructs:
*"Needs its own design pass; do not bolt it onto `fee`/`lines`."* The previous
session bolted on a pricing menu instead of designing the item. This is that pass.

### Decisions taken

- **[DECISION]** A handful of sales services with items underneath, not 22.
- **[DECISION]** An item's **name is its scope**. No per-item inclusion or
  exclusion prose: see §4 for the three reasons, of which the first is that a new
  user must not have to author 600 sentences before issuing anything.
- **[DECISION]** Exclusions stay at **service** level, from the existing shared
  library, opt-out as today. That library is kept, not replaced.
- **[DECISION]** Shape for a second tenant; build nothing for it.
- **[DECISION]** Domain, Hosting, Email, Maintenance and Design are **separate
  services**, not sub-parts of a website. A website engagement *adds* several
  services; it does not absorb them. This is why a service never spans schedules,
  and it is what `contract-system.md` §11 already requires.

---

## 2. The two layers

| Layer | What it is | Count | Table |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Service** | A thing sold. Carries items. | 16 | `services` |
| **Part** | A legal frame: blanks, limits, completion, handover. | 22 | unchanged |

The 22 Parts are **not deleted**. They are good at being a contract frame and
that job does not change. A Service names the frames a contract pulls, via
`partCodes`. A quotation and an invoice never look at a Part.

Moving the catalogue out of `contract/` closes `PRINCIPLES.md` rule 1: a record
used by four document types stops being parented under the first one that used it.

---

## 3. File structure

```
src/lib/domain/
├── service.ts                 Service type, zod, rateUnitOf
├── serviceItem.ts             [NEW] ServiceItem type, zod, assignItemIds
├── seed/
│   ├── services.ts            [NEW] the 16 services and their items
│   └── parts.ts               [MOVED] the 22 legal frames
│                                      (was contract/seed/services.ts)
└── contract/
    ├── blanks.ts              unchanged
    ├── blankMeta.ts           unchanged
    ├── completeness.ts        unchanged
    ├── schedules.ts           unchanged, the four legal frames
    └── seed/libraries.ts      unchanged, E01-E91, I01-I65

docs/service-catalogue.md      this file
```

---

## 4. The types

```ts
// src/lib/domain/serviceItem.ts   [NEW]

/** What a rate is per. */
export type ItemUnit = 'fixed' | 'monthly' | 'perUnit';

export interface ServiceItem {
  /** 'I1', 'I2'… assigned server-side, NEVER reissued. See assignItemIds. */
  id: string;
  /** The line's description. Prints on an invoice and on a quotation. */
  name: string;
  /** One client-facing sentence, printed under the name on a quotation. */
  blurb?: string;
  /** Integer paise. Absent means quoted per engagement. */
  ratePaise?: number;
  unit: ItemUnit;
  /** 'per page', 'per screen', 'per video'. Meaningful for perUnit only. */
  unitLabel?: string;
  /**
   * The rate-card heading this line came from, e.g. 'Foundation system'.
   * A LABEL ONLY: 18 of the 46 groups span several services, so a group can
   * never own an item.
   */
  group?: string;
  /** Overrides the service's SAC where this item classifies differently. */
  sacCode?: string;
  /** The top of a range, for a retainer quoted as a band. */
  rateMaxPaise?: number;
  archived: boolean;
}
```

**There is deliberately no `inclusion` or `exclusion` field.** An item's **name
is its scope**, and that is the decision this whole model turns on. Three
reasons, in the order they matter:

1. **A new user writes nothing.** Setting up means naming items and pricing
   them. Authoring two sentences for 300 items is a week of work before a single
   document can be issued, and most of those sentences would never be read.
2. **The contract stays short.** Twenty ticked items would otherwise add forty
   sentences on top of the Schedule's terms. A named list of twenty
   deliverables is both shorter and easier to check.
3. **The names are already precise.** "Payment gateway integration", "Custom CMS
   development", "Additional standard page" say what they are. A sentence
   restating them adds length, not meaning.

**Exclusions stay where they already work**: attached at *service* level from the
shared library, rendered pre-ticked as excluded, unticked to bring something into
scope (`contract-system.md` §6). That library is 91 lines, shared across every
service, and grows only by the post-project ritual, 3 to 8 lines a project and
then flat. Nothing here is per item, so nothing here grows per item. That is what
bounds it, and it is why the library is **kept rather than replaced**: a generic
line is what makes it reusable across fifteen services.

```ts
// src/lib/domain/service.ts   [CHANGED]

export interface ServiceContent {
  /** Client-facing paragraph. Prints as the quotation service page's blurb. */
  blurb?: string;
  /** Default GST classification; an item may override it. */
  sacCode?: string;
  /** The legal frames a contract pulls when this service is on it. */
  partCodes: string[];
  items: ServiceItem[];
  /** Highest item number ever issued. The never-reissue floor. */
  itemSeq: number;
}

export interface Service extends ServiceContent {
  code: string;               // 'WEB'. Stable, cited by records and documents.
  name: string;
  scheduleKey: ScheduleKey;   // build | retainer | setup | audit
  sortOrder: number;
  archived: boolean;
}
```

**Deleted:** `dependencies` and `pairings` (no reader anywhere in the codebase),
and `menu`/`menuSeq` (replaced by `items`/`itemSeq`).

**Moved to the Part:** `included`, `accountTerms`, `limits`, `limitsNotes`,
`completion`, `receives`, `receivesNotes`, `thirdPartyCosts`, `exclusionIds`,
`clientInputIds`, `fee`, `overview`.

### What each document reads

```
                    ┌──────────────────────────┐
                    │  Service                 │
                    │    items[]               │
                    └────────────┬─────────────┘
      ┌────────────────┬─────────┴──────┬────────────────────┐
      ▼                ▼                ▼                    ▼
   INVOICE         QUOTATION        CONTRACT            CLIENT RECORD
  item.name       item.name        item.name           service.code
  item.sacCode    item.blurb        (as deliverables)  item.id[]
    ?? svc.sacCode  qty × rate     + the Schedule's    agreed ratePaise
  item.ratePaise  item.group        shared terms
  qty               → table heading
```

| Field | Invoice | Quotation | Contract | Client record |
|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| `id` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `name` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | |
| `blurb` | | ✓ | | |
| `ratePaise` | ✓ | ✓ | | ✓ (agreed) |
| `rateMaxPaise` | | ✓ | | |
| `unit` | ✓ | ✓ | | |
| `unitLabel` | | ✓ | | |
| `group` | | ✓ | | |
| `sacCode` | ✓ | | | |

### What a contract actually renders

Vocabulary, because it is easy to slip: a **Part** is not a separate record. It
is a Service *rendered inside a Schedule* as A1, A2, B1 (`contract-system.md` §4
step 5, and `assembly.ts`'s `type ContractPart = ContractService`). There are
**four Schedules in total**, shared by every service, never one per service: ten
build services all render inside Schedule A, because a Shopify build and a custom
build need identical payment and ownership terms.

```
Master agreement                     never changes
Schedule A (Build)                   shared legal terms
  A1  Custom Website                 the Service, rendered as a Part
        Deliverables                 the ticked items        ← NEW
          · Core website setup (5 pages)
          · Custom CMS development
          · Payment gateway integration
          · GSAP motion system
        What is not included         the service's library ids,
          · Copywriting of any kind    pre-ticked as excluded
          · Gateway account approval
  A2  Design
        Deliverables ...
Schedule B (Monthly)
  B1  Website Maintenance ...
```

**The Deliverables list is the only new thing.** Everything below it already
exists and is already reviewed. The list is what makes a contract state what
*this* client bought, which is the gap `ROADMAP.md` §10 reported.

### Editable at source, overridable per contract

Both, and the difference matters:

- **At source** (`/client/services/<code>`): the item's name and rate. Written
  once, reused on every future document.
- **Per contract**: the contract already freezes a copy of everything it
  includes (`CONTEXT.md` §5c), so editing a deliverable there changes that
  contract and nothing else.

The nesting risk raised while designing this is a screen problem, not a model
problem: the scope phase shows the ticked items as one flat list, editable in
place. Nothing in the data requires a dialog inside a sheet inside a drawer, and
a screen that needs five clicks to reach a deliverable has been built wrong.

## 5. The catalogue: 16 services, 293 items

Codes are three or four letters and stable. Rates are **rupees** here for
readability; stored as integer paise (`× 100`).

**Legend:** `fixed` = one-time · `monthly` = per month · `perUnit` = × quantity.
A rate shown `8,000 – 25,000` is a band: `ratePaise` is the low end,
`rateMaxPaise` the high.

## 6. Totals

| Schedule | Services | Items |
|---|---:|---:|
| Build | 6 | 203 |
| Setup | 4 | 15 |
| Retainer | 4 | 51 |
| Audit | 2 | 24 |
| **Total** | **16** | **293** |

293 against the source JSON's 278. Four new items were added for work that is
sold but was never on a card (`DNS` I3, `HOST` I4, `MAIL` I2, `ANLY` I5), and
roughly 17 lines appear twice on purpose, where the same work is sold both inside
a build and standalone as an audit (question 3, §8). Seven lines that were
duplicated *by mistake* in the first draft have been removed: three analytics
items off `WEB`, and four maintenance items off `MNT`.

**Item ids are never reissued, so a service's `itemSeq` is a high-water mark and
not a count.** `WEB` carries 52 items with `itemSeq: 55`; `MNT` carries 7 with
`itemSeq: 11`. Those gaps are the removed duplicates, and closing them would be
the bug the rule exists to prevent.

## 7. Worked example: the Colorist quotation

Proving the model reproduces a document already sent to a client.

| Printed line | Service | Item | Rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Infrastructure Set-up | WEB | I4 Core website setup | 20,000 ≈ 25,000 |
| Web design | DSGN | I3 Multi-page website design | 15,000 |
| SEO/AEO/GEO | WEB | I30 SEO foundation setup | 15,000 |
| Data Privacy (cookies) | ANLY | I5 Cookie consent | 5,000 |
| Domain Services | DNS | I1 Domain & DNS configuration | 5,000 ≈ 4,000 |
| CMS (scalable) | WEB | I47 Custom CMS development | 25,000 |
| Custom booking section | WEB | I23 Booking & scheduling | 20,000 |
| Payment Portal (Razorpay) | WEB | I46 Payment gateway integration | 20,000 |
| Interactivity and motion | WEB | I11 GSAP motion system | 30,000 |
| Motion design & prototype | DSGN | I32 Premium motion system | 15,000 |
| WhatsApp Automation | AUTO | I9 WhatsApp automation (set-up) | 50,000 |
| Business Email | MAIL | I2 Google Workspace setup | 5,000 |
| *Recurring:* Business Email | none | third-party, at actual | 200/mo |
| *Recurring:* Hosting | none | third-party, at actual | 2,870/mo |
| *Recurring:* WhatsApp BSP | none | third-party, at actual | 1,500-5,000/mo |

**Two findings.**

1. **Quoted rates differ from list rates** (booking 20,000 quoted against 18,000
   list; motion 30,000 against 20,000). Expected, and the model allows it: a list
   price is what the studio quotes *from*. The document stores its own rate; the
   catalogue only seeds it.
2. **Every recurring row is a third-party cost, not a Qera item.** Hosting,
   Workspace and the BSP platform are billed at actual and belong on the
   quotation's recurring page, which has its own `RecurringLine` type.
   **This confirms `HOST` sells the set-up and never the monthly charge.**

## 8. Questions, resolved 19 September 2026

Nine of the ten are closed. Recorded here rather than deleted, so the reasoning
survives.

| # | Question | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `APP` separate from `DSGN`? | **Separate.** 16 services. |
| 2 | `ANLY` I1-I3 duplicated on `WEB`? | **`ANLY` only.** Removed from `WEB`. |
| 3 | `AUD` overlap with other services? | **Keep it.** An audit sold on its own is its own item, even where the work also appears inside a build. |
| 4 | `MNT` tiers? | **Not tiers.** Five kinds of work, each a band. The three real tiers were `AIOP`'s all along. |
| 5 | `AIOP` I6-I8 duplicate `MNT`? | **Renamed,** and they are the only copies: `MNT` I2-I4 were a filing error here, now removed. |
| 6 | Five unpriced items | **Still open.** See below. |
| 7 | `SOC` engagement at two prices? | **Both real.** Organic posts against ad creative; renamed to say so. |
| 8 | AI tiers at two prices? | **Both kept.** |
| 9 | Spline at 4,000? | **80,000.** A missing zero on the card. |
| 10 | Item inclusion / exclusion wording | **Dropped entirely.** An item's name is its scope; see §4. |

### Still open

**Three items carry no rate**, because they appear on no rate card. Two are work
that is certainly sold and simply was never priced on paper; the third is on a
real quotation and needs confirming.

| Service | Item | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `DNS` | I3 Domain transfer or migration | Confirm it is a thing you sell, then price |
| `HOST` | I4 VPS / private Linux provisioning | Likewise |
| `ANLY` | I5 Cookie consent & data privacy | Quoted at 5,000 on the Colorist document |

`MAIL` I2 was on this list and is not any more: §5 carries the ₹5,000 the
Colorist quotation charged for it, which is a real figure from a real document
rather than a rate card's, and that is what the seed loads.

An item with no rate is valid: `ratePaise` absent means **quoted per
engagement**, and the document asks for a figure when the item is ticked. So
these do not block the build; they only mean three lines get typed by hand until
somebody sets a list price.

## 9. Build order

One commit per step, `npm test` green between each.

| # | Step | Touches a document? |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `serviceItem.ts` and its tests. Pure, no consumers. Prove the id rule first. | no |
| 2 | Move the 22 to `seed/parts.ts`, renamed `PARTS`. Imports only. | no |
| 3 | `items[]` and `partCodes` on `ServiceContent`; drop `menu`, `menuSeq`, `dependencies`, `pairings`. The server action's sections follow. | no |
| 4 | `ItemsEditor` (was `MenuEditor`): name, rate, unit, group, SAC, blurb. No wording fields. | no |
| 5 | Seed the 16 services and 293 items from §5, and **retire the 22 old catalogue rows** (see below). | no |
| 6 | Invoice reads items. | **yes** |
| 7 | Quotation reads items. | **yes** |
| 8 | Contract prints the Deliverables list. | **yes** |

Steps 1 to 5 change no document's appearance, which the format freeze requires.
Steps 6 to 8 each change one, which is why they are three commits and not one.

### Step 5 is the one with a migration in it

The 22 rows are in the database now, carrying contract prose. Seeding 16 more
without retiring them leaves 38 rows in one catalogue, and the picker would offer
both "Custom web build" and "Custom Website".

**They are not deleted.** A finalized contract froze a copy of its Parts
(`CONTEXT.md` §5c), so nothing already issued depends on the live rows; but
`archived` is the house answer for removing something from a list, and the
`services` table already has the column. So: seed the 16, archive the 22, and
leave the prose where a future contract build can still read it through
`partCodes`.

Draft contracts are the case to check, not finalized ones. A draft resolves its
client live but holds its own `parts` copy, so an archived source row does not
empty it. Worth confirming against a real draft before the commit lands.

### Verification

- `npm test` green at every step.
- **Prove the id rule fails when broken:** delete an item, add another, assert
  the new id is not the dead one. Watch it go red without `itemSeq`.
- **A finalized contract renders byte-identically** after step 2, and again
  after step 5. Compare `contractBlocks` output for a fixture before and after.
- **An open draft contract still lists its Parts** after step 5's archive.
- `npm run test:e2e` after step 7: item blurbs make service pages taller and
  `e2e/quotation.spec.ts` asserts that no page overflows.
- In a browser: add an item with a rate and a SAC, then raise an invoice for a
  client engaged on that service and confirm the line carries the name, the rate
  and the SAC (Rule 46(g), currently unsatisfied).

### Not in scope

- **No multi-tenancy.** `maturity.md` scores it 0 and calls it correctly
  unbuilt. The catalogue is shaped as importable data so that work is later a
  seed file rather than a remodel.
- **No quotation flow rebuild.** Deferred pending this; it reopens afterwards.
- **No payment-phasing change.** `ROADMAP.md` §10's second gap.
- **No new legal text.** `contract-system.md` §1: adding a service must never
  require writing new legal text. Items contribute a list of names; the terms
  stay on the Schedule and the exclusions stay in the shared library.

## 1. Corrections — apply before templating anything

These are errors in the existing Zaib contract (12 May 2026). If templated as-is they
propagate into every contract ever generated. Do not retrofit the Zaib document itself —
it is a signed historical record. Fix the template.

### Errors

| Error | Correct |
|---|---|
| Signature blocks inverted — "Qera Studio (First party) / Name: ZaibQ Studioh" appears in all three documents | First party block carries Qera Private Limited. Second party carries the client. |
| "both Parties acknowledge that they **will** read, understood" | "have read, understood, and agreed" |
| Client name inconsistent: "ZaibQ Stuioh" vs "ZaibQ Studioh" | Single source, one blank, no free typing |
| Heading typo "CLIENT RESPONSIBILITES" | RESPONSIBILITIES |
| Heading typo "GOVERNING LAW & JURSIDICTION" | JURISDICTION |
| Entity mismatch — "Qera Studio" in PDF, "Qera Private Limited" in tool | Qera Private Limited, everywhere |
| Email mismatch — hello@qera.studio in PDF, sales@qera.studio in tool | Pick one. Recommend hello@ for contracts. |
| Schedule A says "under four (4) weeks", milestone table runs three weeks | One source. Timeline is a blank; the table derives from it. |
| Schedule B: monthly advance retainer, then "Project may follow a 100% advance completion structure" | Delete the second sentence. It contradicts the first and means nothing. |

### Gaps to add to the master agreement

Six clauses the current text does not carry:

1. **Client indemnity** — for materials the client supplied: IP claims, factual accuracy, regulatory compliance. Current text assigns responsibility but contains no true indemnity.
2. **Late payment interest** — a stated monthly rate. Without it the suspension clause has no teeth.
3. **Non-solicitation** — of Qera's team, subcontractors and specialists, for a stated period after engagement ends.
4. **Data protection** — a reference clause. Needed once customer data is handled, and UAE clients raise it.
5. **Termination for convenience** — with a defined kill fee. Current text only covers termination for breach.
6. **Credential and account return on termination** — currently absent entirely. This is the largest exposure on social and infrastructure work.

## 2. Master Service Agreement

Complete. Read together with the four Schedules and the Parts appended to them.

**Placement rule.** A clause belongs in this Agreement where it applies identically regardless of
the kind of work. A clause belongs in a Schedule where it differs between a one-time build, a
monthly engagement, a setup and an advisory engagement. Where the same words appear in two or
more Schedules, they move here.

---

> # MASTER SERVICE AGREEMENT
>
> This Agreement is made on `[agreement_date]`
>
> **BETWEEN**
>
> **QERA PRIVATE LIMITED**, a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013, having its
> registered office at C-204, MGI Gharaunda, Raj Nagar Extension, Ghaziabad 201017, Uttar Pradesh,
> India (hereinafter "**Qera**", which expression shall include its successors and permitted
> assigns), of the First Part;
>
> **AND**
>
> `[client_legal_name]`, having its principal place of business at `[client_address]`
> (hereinafter the "**Client**", which expression shall include its successors and permitted
> assigns), of the Second Part.
>
> Qera and the Client are hereinafter referred to individually as a "**Party**" and collectively
> as the "**Parties**".

### 1. Definitions and Interpretation

**1.1** In this Agreement, unless the context otherwise requires:

"**Additional Work**" means any work not expressly specified within an approved Part or Proposal.

"**Agreement**" means this Master Service Agreement together with all Schedules, Parts, Proposals
and written amendments executed by the Parties.

"**Client Inputs**" means the information, materials, assets, credentials, approvals and access
which the Client is required to supply under an applicable Part.

"**Deliverables**" means the final approved outputs specified in an applicable Part.

"**Part**" means a service specification appended to a Schedule, describing the scope of a
particular service.

"**Proposal**" means the commercial quotation setting out fees, timelines and engagement-specific
particulars provided to the Client.

"**Retained Materials**" has the meaning given at clause 11.2.

"**Revision**" has the meaning given at clause 7.1.

"**Schedule**" means any of the Build, Monthly, Setup or Advice Schedules forming part of this
Agreement.

"**Services**" means the services performed by Qera under this Agreement.

"**Third-Party Services**" means any platform, application programming interface, hosting
provider, model provider, software tool, plugin, advertising platform, infrastructure service or
technology not owned or controlled by Qera.

**1.2** Headings are for convenience only and shall not affect construction. References to a
clause are references to a clause of this Agreement. Words importing the singular include the
plural and vice versa. "Including" means including without limitation. A reference to writing
includes email.

**1.3** Any period expressed in days shall mean calendar days unless expressed as working days,
in which case Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays at the place of performance shall be
excluded.

### 2. Structure and Order of Precedence

**2.1** This Agreement establishes the legal and operational framework governing all Services
provided by Qera to the Client. It applies to every engagement between the Parties and continues
in force notwithstanding the completion of any individual engagement.

**2.2** Each engagement shall be governed by this Agreement together with the applicable Schedule,
the Parts appended to it, and any approved Proposal.

**2.3** In the event of inconsistency, the order of precedence shall be: (a) the approved
Proposal; (b) the applicable Part; (c) the applicable Schedule; and (d) this Agreement.

**2.4** No engagement shall commence, and no obligation to perform shall arise, until the Parties
have executed the applicable Schedule and Qera has received the payment and Client Inputs
required thereunder.

### 3. Mutual Obligations

**3.1** This Agreement imposes obligations upon both Parties. Each Party shall perform its
obligations in good faith and shall not unreasonably withhold or delay any approval, consent or
cooperation required of it.

**3.2** Qera shall:

(a) perform the Services with reasonable skill, care and diligence, and to the standard ordinarily
    expected of a competent professional studio in its field;

(b) deliver the Deliverables described in each applicable Part, and shall notify the Client in
    writing where any described Deliverable is not achievable, together with the reasons;

(c) notify the Client in writing without undue delay where any agreed date is at risk, stating the
    cause and a revised date;

(d) quote any Additional Work in writing and obtain the Client's written approval prior to
    commencing it, and shall not invoice the Client for work not so approved;

(e) remedy, at its own cost, any defect in the Deliverables arising from its own act or omission
    and reported within the applicable support or correction period;

(f) give the Client written notice and a reasonable opportunity to remedy the cause before
    suspending performance of the Services;

(g) treat the Client's non-public business information as confidential in accordance with clause
    13, and shall not use Client data to train artificial intelligence models;

(h) procure that every account, domain name and subscription created in connection with the
    Services is registered in the Client's name, so that the Client's ownership of its own
    infrastructure is not contingent upon the continuation of this Agreement;

(i) deliver all materials to which the Client is entitled promptly upon payment of the sums
    properly due in respect of them; and

(j) remove its own access to the Client's systems and accounts promptly upon request or upon
    termination.

**3.3** The Client shall:

(a) supply the Client Inputs specified in each applicable Part, in usable form, so as to enable
    performance of the Services;

(b) respond to submissions and requests for approval within the periods specified in the
    applicable Schedule or Part;

(c) pay each invoice in accordance with its terms;

(d) warrant that it holds all necessary rights, licences and consents in respect of any material
    it supplies to Qera;

(e) nominate a single individual with authority to approve Deliverables and give instructions on
    its behalf; and

(f) raise any concern regarding performance in writing and without undue delay, so that it may be
    addressed at the earliest practicable stage.

### 4. Scope and Additional Work

**4.1** Qera shall perform the Services specified in the approved Proposal and applicable Part.

**4.2** Any work, feature, request, integration, deliverable, modification, enhancement or
strategic expansion not expressly included within the approved written scope shall constitute
Additional Work.

**4.3** No conversation, exploratory discussion, assumption, informal message or conceptual
reference shall operate to vary the scope, fees or timelines of any engagement unless confirmed
in writing by both Parties.

**4.4** Additional Work may result in revised fees, timelines, milestones and resource
allocation. Qera may decline Additional Work which it is not appropriately placed to deliver. No
Additional Work shall commence unless approved in writing.

### 5. Communication and Notices

**5.1** Operational communication may be conducted by email, messaging platform, project
management tool or meeting, as the Parties find convenient.

**5.2** Approvals, variations to scope, commercial confirmations and formal notices shall be
confirmed by email. No instruction, representation or discussion conducted otherwise shall
operate to vary this Agreement, and neither Party shall be bound by any purported agreement not
so confirmed.

**5.3** Formal notices shall be sent to the email addresses stated in the applicable Schedule and
shall be deemed received on the next working day following transmission, absent evidence of
delivery failure.

**5.4** Qera shall not be liable for any misunderstanding arising from fragmented, inconsistent or
undocumented communication conducted otherwise than in accordance with this clause.

### 6. Feedback and Approval

**6.1** Where a Schedule or Part specifies a period for feedback, the Client shall provide
consolidated written feedback within that period.

**6.2** Where the Client does not respond within the specified period, the relevant submission
shall be deemed approved, so as to permit the Services to continue without interruption. Qera
shall issue a written reminder prior to treating any submission as approved by default.

**6.3** Either Party may request a reasonable extension of any period specified under this clause
in circumstances of genuine emergency, and such request shall not be unreasonably refused.

### 7. Revisions

**7.1** A "Revision" means the refinement of work already approved in direction, including
adjustment to spacing, sizing, wording, colour or layout, and the correction of errors.

**7.2** A Revision does not include a new concept, a change of direction, restructured navigation,
additional pages, additional functionality or a redesign. Such work constitutes Additional Work.

**7.3** The number of Revision rounds included is specified in the applicable Schedule and Part.

**7.4** The correction of any error attributable to Qera shall not be counted as a Revision round
and shall be undertaken at Qera's own cost.

**7.5** The Client acknowledges that branding, design, strategy, content, motion, visual identity
and comparable creative services involve subjective interpretation and judgment. Deliverables
shall be assessed against approved briefs, agreed objectives, approved references, technical
feasibility and commercial scope, and not against evolving personal preference alone. Qera shall
use reasonable endeavours to align with the Client's vision within the approved Revision
structure.

### 8. Fees, Invoicing and Payment

**8.1** Fees, retainers, milestone structures and commercial terms are specified in the approved
Proposal and applicable Part.

**8.2** All taxes, duties, payment gateway charges, transfer fees, international transaction fees
and government-imposed charges shall be borne by the Client, save where expressly stated

applicable rate.

**8.3** Invoices shall be payable within the period stated thereon or, where no period is stated,

**8.4** Where any sum remains unpaid after its due date, Qera shall notify the Client in writing.
Interest shall accrue on any sum outstanding more than `[15 days]` after its due date at the rate
of `[1.5%]` per month, or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, whichever is lower,
calculated from the due date until payment. Qera may waive such interest at its discretion.

**8.5** Suspension of performance for non-payment is governed by the applicable Schedule. Qera
shall not withhold any Deliverable, source material or access in respect of which the sums
properly due have been paid.

**8.6** All sums payable are exclusive of Third-Party Costs, which are governed by clause 9.

### 9. Third-Party Costs

**9.1** Platform subscriptions, hosting, domain fees, licences, paid applications, model and
application programming interface usage, advertising spend, stock assets, typeface licences and

**9.3** Where, by agreement, Qera discharges any such cost on the Client's behalf, it shall be

**9.4** Qera shall not be obliged to fund, advance or hold any sum on the Client's behalf, and

**10.1** Title to and all intellectual property rights in the final approved Deliverables shall

19 of the Copyright Act, 1957, and shall take effect upon receipt of full payment. Qera shall

**10.3** The Client retains ownership of all material supplied by it to Qera, and grants Qera a

remain the property of Qera.

**10.5** Transfer of source files, editable assets, repositories, automation workflows, design

**11.1** Each Part specifies the materials the Client shall receive. Where the Client requires

resale or use in any separate project.

reason, so that the Client's ability to operate and modify the Deliverables is not prejudiced by

**12.1** Qera may display completed work in its portfolio, case studies, marketing materials,

**12.3** The right at clause 12.2 forms part of the consideration for the fees stated in the

**12.4** The obligation at clause 12.2 shall subsist for so long as the delivered property remains
substantially in the form delivered by Qera.

### 13. Confidentiality

**13.1** Each Party shall keep confidential all non-public business, operational, technical,
strategic and financial information of the other Party disclosed in connection with this
Agreement, and shall not disclose it to any third party save as permitted by this clause.

**13.2** Disclosure is permitted (a) to personnel, subcontractors and professional advisers who
require it for the performance of this Agreement and who are bound by equivalent obligations;
(b) where required by law, regulation or court order; and (c) where the receiving Party can
demonstrate the information was already public, already known to it, or independently developed.

**13.3** This clause shall survive termination of this Agreement for a period of `[3 years]`, save
in respect of information constituting a trade secret, in respect of which the obligation shall
subsist indefinitely.

### 14. Data Protection

**14.1** Each Party shall comply with applicable data protection law, including the Digital
Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.

**14.2** Where Qera processes personal data on the Client's behalf in the course of performing the
Services, the Client shall be the Data Fiduciary and Qera the Data Processor. Qera shall process

**14.3** Qera shall implement reasonable technical and organisational measures to protect personal
data in its possession, and shall notify the Client without undue delay upon becoming aware of any

**14.4** The Client warrants that it has obtained all necessary consents and provided all
necessary notices in respect of personal data supplied to Qera, and that such supply does not
contravene applicable law.

**14.5** Upon termination, Qera shall, at the Client's written election, return or securely delete
personal data in its possession, save where retention is required by law.

**14.6** Where the Services require personal data to be processed by Third-Party Services, such
processing shall be governed by the terms of the relevant provider, which Qera does not control.

**15.1** Qera may subcontract any portion of the Services, engage freelancers, specialists or

**17.1** The Client acknowledges that artificial intelligence and automation systems may produce
inaccurate, incomplete, probabilistic or non-repeatable outputs, may alter their behaviour over

**17.2** Qera does not warrant factual accuracy, originality, consistency, uninterrupted
operation, permanent compatibility or deterministic output of any artificial intelligence or

**17.3** The Client shall review and approve all artificial intelligence or automation-generated

**17.4** Qera does not use Client data to train artificial intelligence models. Third-party

**18.1** Qera does not guarantee revenue growth, conversion rates, lead volume, follower growth,

**19.1** Each Party warrants that it has full power and authority to enter into and perform this

**20.2** Qera shall indemnify the Client against all losses, damages, costs and reasonable legal

**21.1** Neither Party shall be liable for indirect, incidental, consequential, special or punitive

**21.3** Liability arising from Third-Party Services, platform restrictions, infrastructure
failures, artificial intelligence systems or external providers is excluded to the maximum extent

**21.4** Nothing in this Agreement excludes or limits liability for (a) fraud or fraudulent

**21.5** The limitations at this clause reflect the allocation of risk between the Parties having

### 22. Force Majeure

**22.1** Neither Party shall be liable for any delay or failure to perform arising from events
beyond its reasonable control, including natural disaster, internet or infrastructure outage,
government restriction, cyberattack, platform outage, labour dispute, war, civil unrest, epidemic,
pandemic or regulatory change.

endeavours to mitigate the effect. Where such event continues for more than `[60 days]`, either

### 23. Non-Solicitation

**23.1** During the term of this Agreement and for `[12 months]` following its termination,
neither Party shall directly solicit for employment or engagement any employee, subcontractor or
freelancer of the other Party who has been materially involved in the Services, without the other

**23.2** This clause shall not apply to any response to a general public advertisement not
specifically directed at such person.

**23.3** Where this clause is breached, the breaching Party shall pay the other a sum equal to
`[50%]` of the relevant person's annual remuneration, as a genuine pre-estimate of loss.

### 24. Suspension and Termination

**24.1** Either Party may terminate an engagement in accordance with the applicable Schedule.

**24.2** Either Party may terminate this Agreement or any engagement immediately by written notice
where the other Party (a) commits a material breach which is incapable of remedy, or which is not
remedied within `[15 days]` of written notice requiring remedy; (b) becomes insolvent, enters
liquidation or has a receiver appointed; or (c) ceases or threatens to cease carrying on business.

**24.3** Qera may suspend or terminate immediately where the Client's conduct is abusive or
unlawful, where the Client instructs Qera to act unlawfully, or where continued performance would
expose Qera to material reputational or legal risk.

**24.4** The Client may terminate immediately where Qera has materially and persistently failed to
perform the Services in accordance with clause 3.2(a) and has not remedied such failure within

**24.5** Termination of one engagement shall not terminate any other engagement or this Agreement,
unless expressly stated.

### 25. Consequences of Termination

**25.1** Upon termination for any reason, Qera shall within `[14 days]`:

(a) deliver to the Client all Deliverables for which payment has been made in full;

(b) transfer or release every account, domain name, subscription and credential held on the
    Client's behalf;

(c) remove its own access from the Client's systems, accounts and platforms; and

(d) deliver a written record of the configuration of any system it has operated, sufficient to
    enable a competent third party to assume its operation.

**25.2** The Client shall pay all sums due for work performed and resources committed as at the
date of termination, calculated in accordance with the applicable Schedule.

**25.3** Any sum held by Qera in excess of the amount payable under clause 25.2 shall be refunded
to the Client within `[14 days]`.

**25.4** Clauses 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 19, 20, 21, 23, 25, 26 and 27, together with any other
provision which by its nature is intended to survive, shall survive termination.

### 26. Dispute Resolution

**26.1** Where any dispute arises, the Parties shall first attempt to resolve it by good-faith
discussion between senior representatives within `[30 days]` of written notice of the dispute.

**26.2** Where the dispute is not so resolved, it shall be referred to and finally resolved by
arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, before a sole arbitrator appointed
by agreement between the Parties or, failing agreement within `[30 days]`, by the competent court.
The seat of arbitration shall be Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh, and the language shall be English.

**26.3** Nothing in this clause shall prevent either Party from seeking urgent interim or
injunctive relief from a competent court.

### 27. Governing Law and Jurisdiction

**27.1** This Agreement and any dispute arising from it shall be governed by and construed in
accordance with the laws of India.

**27.2** Subject to clause 26, the courts at Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh shall have exclusive
jurisdiction.

### 28. General

**28.1 Entire agreement.** This Agreement, together with the applicable Schedules, Parts,
Proposals and written amendments, constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties and
supersedes all prior discussions, verbal understandings and representations.

**28.2 Amendment.** No amendment shall be effective unless made in writing and agreed by both
Parties.

**28.3 Assignment.** Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the other's prior written
consent, save that either Party may assign to a successor in title to substantially the whole of
its business.

**28.4 Waiver.** No failure or delay in exercising any right shall constitute a waiver of it.

**28.5 Severability.** Where any provision is held invalid or unenforceable, the remainder shall
continue in full force, and the invalid provision shall be replaced by a valid provision achieving
as nearly as possible the same commercial effect.

**28.6 Relationship.** Nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture, agency or
employment relationship between the Parties.

**28.7 Third-party rights.** No person who is not a Party shall have any right to enforce any
provision of this Agreement.

**28.8 Counterparts and electronic execution.** This Agreement may be executed in counterparts and
by electronic signature, each of which shall constitute an original and together shall constitute
one instrument.

---

### Drafting notes for the Master Service Agreement

The Agreement above is complete and supersedes the May 2026 document in full. The following were
defects in that document and have been corrected here; the renderer must not reintroduce them.

- Signature blocks were inverted, the first-party block carrying the Client's name. Clause 29
  renders both blocks from the contract record.
- "both Parties acknowledge that they will read, understood" is corrected throughout.
- The Client's name appeared in two spellings within one document. It is now rendered once from
  the client record.
- "RESPONSIBILITES" and "JURSIDICTION" are corrected.
- The entity is Qera Private Limited. "Qera Studio" is a trading name and appears in prose and in
  the attribution credit only, never in the parties or execution blocks.
- Contact email and telephone number must be reconciled before use. The May 2026 document and the
  current tool disagree on both. Store one of each in a single settings record.
- Schedule B of the May 2026 document stated monthly advance billing and then a "100% advance
  completion structure". The contradiction is not carried forward.

**Blanks requiring confirmation before first use:**

```
late_payment_interest      1.5% per month          verify against applicable law
confidentiality_term       3 years
non_solicit_term           12 months
non_solicit_sum            50% of annual remuneration
force_majeure_termination  60 days
cure_period                15 days
dispute_discussion_period  30 days
invoice_term               7 days
```

**Before use.** This Agreement and the four Schedules should be reviewed as a single package by an
Indian commercial lawyer. The twenty-two Parts are scope documents and do not require the same
review. Nothing in this file constitutes legal advice.

**Open question — jurisdiction.** Governing law is India and the seat is Ghaziabad, matching the
registered entity. The target market is Dubai-based. Clause 26 provides arbitration, which is
enforceable against a UAE counterparty under the New York Convention and is materially more useful
than litigation in Ghaziabad would be. Where a UAE client objects to the seat, moving the seat to
the DIFC while retaining Indian governing law is the usual middle ground and should be priced as a
negotiated concession rather than conceded by default.

**Separate from this Agreement.** Performing work from the UAE without a UAE trade licence is a
licensing question for the CA, not a contractual one. It does not affect this text.

## 3b. Schedule 2 — Monthly

> **Schedule [letter] — Monthly**
>
> This Schedule forms part of the Master Service Agreement between Qera Private Limited and
> the Client. It governs all work delivered on a recurring monthly basis for a recurring fee.

### [letter]0.1 What this schedule covers

The parts attached to this Schedule describe what is delivered each month. This Schedule
describes how that work is billed, approved, paused, owned and ended.

This Schedule shall be read together with the Master Service Agreement, which governs the mutual
obligations of the Parties, feedback and approval, Revisions, third-party costs, Retained
Materials and attribution.

In the event of inconsistency, the applicable Part shall prevail over this Schedule, and this
Schedule shall prevail over the Master Service Agreement.

### [letter]0.2 Fee and billing

The monthly fee for each part is stated within that part. Fees are payable in advance, before
the cycle they cover begins.

The first cycle begins on the date the first payment is received. Each subsequent cycle begins
on the same date of the following month. Where that date does not exist in a given month, the
cycle begins on the last day of that month.

An alternative billing date may be agreed in writing. Where a billing date is changed, the
first affected cycle is charged pro rata.

### [letter]0.3 Term and renewal

The engagement runs month to month from the first cycle and renews automatically unless ended
under [letter]0.11.

There is no minimum term unless stated in the part.

### [letter]0.4 Late payment and pause

Where payment is not received by the cycle start date, a grace period of `[7 days]` applies.

Where payment remains outstanding following the grace period, Qera Private Limited shall notify
the Client in writing prior to suspending performance. Where the sum remains outstanding, work
under this Schedule may be suspended. During any such suspension no work shall be performed, no
content shall be published, and no monitoring or response obligation shall subsist.

Work resumes on receipt of payment. Where a pause has occurred, the billing anniversary moves
to the date work resumed.

### [letter]0.5 Monthly capacity

Each part states the volume included in a cycle — items, posts, hours, or another stated unit.

Capacity is scoped per cycle. Where capacity is unused because the Client did not supply
inputs or approvals in time, the unused portion carries forward for up to `[2]` further
cycles and then lapses.

Carried-forward capacity is delivered subject to available scheduling and does not create an
obligation to exceed normal monthly output in any single cycle.

Unused and carried-forward capacity shall lapse upon termination. Where capacity has gone unused
by reason of any act or omission of Qera Private Limited, the Client may elect to take delivery
of such capacity during the notice period or to receive a credit in respect of it.

Capacity is not transferable between parts.

### [letter]0.6 Planning, approval and turnaround

Work under this Schedule follows an agreed monthly cycle of planning, production, review and
delivery. The Client provides a named approver.

The Client provides consolidated written feedback within `[48 hours]` of receiving any
submission. Where no feedback is received in that window, the submission is treated as
approved.

Where approvals are delayed, delivery within that cycle may be reduced accordingly and the
undelivered portion is treated under [letter]0.5.

### [letter]0.7 Revisions

Each Part includes reasonable Revision within the approved direction and plan, as defined in the
Master Service Agreement.

The reworking of any item following publication shall constitute Additional Work, the original
having been delivered and used. Where any item has been published containing an error
attributable to Qera Private Limited, such error shall be corrected at Qera Private Limited's own
cost.

### [letter]0.8 Credentials and account access

The Client provides access to each platform in scope, and retains ownership of every account.

Qera Private Limited holds access only for the duration of the engagement and for the purpose
of performing the Services. Access is not shared outside the engagement team.

Where an account is created by Qera Private Limited on the Client's behalf, it is created in
the Client's name and belongs to the Client from creation.

The Client remains responsible for maintaining its own recovery access to every platform,
including recovery email, recovery phone number and any second-factor method.

Qera Private Limited is not liable for account restriction, suspension, loss of access or
enforcement action taken by a platform.

### [letter]0.9 Ownership of content

Final approved content delivered under this Schedule may be used by the Client for its
business and marketing purposes, from the cycle in which it was paid for.

Working files, project files, raw and unused assets, internal templates, planning systems and
operational frameworks remain the property of Qera Private Limited unless the part states
otherwise.

### [letter]0.10 What is handed over on ending

Within `[14 days]` of the engagement ending, Qera Private Limited will:

- remove its own access from every platform in scope
- deliver all final approved content produced and paid for under the engagement, including
  content produced but not yet published
- deliver the final assets connected to those deliverables

Where the Client requires working files, unused concepts or planning material, Qera Private
Limited shall supply such materials as it reasonably can. Materials incorporating Retained
Materials shall be governed by clause 11 of the Master Service Agreement, and in no circumstances
shall the Client be left without the materials necessary to continue its own operations.

### [letter]0.11 Ending the engagement

Either Party may end the engagement by giving `[15 days]` written notice.

Notice takes effect at the end of the cycle in which the notice period expires. Fees for that
cycle remain payable in full and are not refundable.

Qera Private Limited may suspend or end the engagement immediately in cases of non-payment,
abusive conduct, unlawful instruction, or material breach.

### [letter]0.12 No guarantee of outcome

Qera Private Limited does not guarantee reach, engagement, follower growth, virality,
conversions, revenue, lead volume, search ranking, verification or monetisation.

Platforms change their algorithms, policies and behaviour without notice. Qera Private Limited
commits to consistent execution against the agreed plan, not to a business outcome.
